long_biography.plain_text:
Turning a small Nigerian trading house into a diversified industrial group has defined Sunil Vaswani's career. He returned from university in London at 21 and persuaded his father to replace slow-moving sundries with high-volume rice, wheat and sugar. The faster turnover funded fishing vessels and a broader food-distribution network, giving the family business a platform for further investment.

Automotive distribution became Stallion's first route beyond trading, followed by vehicle assembly, local food processing, agriculture, steel, plastics, packaging and logistics. The shift preserved the commodity engine while reducing dependence on any single line of business. He remained chairman while his brothers assumed senior operating roles across the group. Vaswani continues to direct a business centred on West Africa but headquartered in Dubai, with operations spread across 18 countries.
